title: Integrated Whole-Brain Explorer and Capstone
subtitle: Navigate the complete anatomy atlas and integrate structures, pathways, territories, networks and clinical patterns
altText: Accessible chalkboard-style whole-brain overview showing bilateral cortex around deep nuclei and ventricles, connected to brainstem and cerebellum by white-matter pathways, with vascular, functional-network and lesion overlays and labelled atlas entry points.
learningObjectives: Navigate from a whole-brain overview to every completed Interactive Anatomy structure.
Integrate cortical, subcortical, cerebellar and brainstem anatomy through white-matter pathways and distributed networks.
Compare vascular, functional and lesion overlays while accounting for laterality and healthy variation.
Form qualified clinical hypotheses that combine location, pathway, network, vascular territory and context.

sections.explainSimply: The brain works as one connected system. Start with the whole-brain map, choose an anatomical family, add an overlay and open any detailed atlas structure.
sections.explainLikePsychologist: Cognition, emotion and behaviour depend on interactions among cortical regions, deep nuclei, brainstem, cerebellum and connecting fibres. The capstone keeps localisation useful without reducing a person to one region.
sections.advancedClinicalDetail: Integrated localisation combines tissue compartment, laterality, tract course, network topology, vascular distribution and lesion mechanism. Cortico-subcortical loops, cerebello-thalamo-cortical pathways, ascending arousal systems and commissural, association and projection fibres make remote or distributed effects expected rather than exceptional.
sections.thinkOfItLike: A city map can show neighbourhoods, rail lines, utilities, traffic zones and disruptions on the same base map; each layer answers a different question, but no layer explains the city alone.
sections.whyPsychologistsCare: The explorer links test findings and behaviour to plausible systems while preserving differential diagnosis, development, reserve, medications, fatigue, culture, psychosocial context and performance validity.
sections.whenItGoesWrong: A focal cortical lesion may also disconnect fibres and depress remote nodes; a small deep lesion may affect compact motor, sensory and cognitive pathways; brainstem or cerebellar injury can alter cortical function through long loops; vascular and degenerative disease may cross several networks.
sections.clinicalPearl: Move through five questions: where is the change, which fibres pass there, which networks depend on them, which vascular or disease mechanism fits, and what evidence could disconfirm the hypothesis?
sections.practicalExample: For sudden aphasia and right face-arm weakness, compare hemispheres, open the cortical and white-matter domains, add vascular and lesion overlays, then navigate to arterial territories and lesion mapping. Treat the result as an urgent left-network vascular hypothesis requiring examination and imaging.
sections.limitationsCautions: This schematic explorer does not represent individual anatomy, imaging resolution, perfusion, temporal evolution or every connection. Overlay convergence strengthens a hypothesis but does not establish diagnosis, causality, prognosis or psychological meaning.

anatomy.position: Integrated whole-brain overview spanning bilateral cerebral cortex, deep nuclei, limbic and diencephalic structures, ventricles and meninges, brainstem, cerebellum, cranial nerves, white matter and cerebral vasculature.
anatomy.spatialRelationships: Cortical areas surround and connect with subcortical nuclei; projection, association and commissural fibres link hemispheres and levels; the brainstem joins cerebrum, cerebellum, spinal and cranial systems; arterial territories overlap and vary.
functions: navigate to every completed anatomy structure
inspect vascular, functional and lesion overlays
anatomy.bloodSupply: ACA, MCA and PCA cortical territories interact with deep perforators and vertebrobasilar, PICA, AICA and SCA territories. Watersheds and borders vary; venous, haemorrhagic and nonvascular mechanisms require different reasoning.
anatomy.lesionEffects: Clinical effects reflect local tissue injury, affected fibres, network disconnection, laterality, vascular distribution, diaschisis and time. Similar symptoms may arise from different sites, and similar lesions may produce different presentations.
neurologicalPresentations: altered arousal, memory or executive control
psychologicalPresentations: changes in attention, language, memory or social cognition
altered motivation, affect regulation or self-monitoring
variable disability shaped by reserve and environment
anatomy.clinicalSignificance: A whole-brain framework helps clinicians combine focal localisation with pathway, network and vascular reasoning, select detailed atlas views and state uncertainty without using anatomy as a stand-alone diagnosis.

explorerParts.label: Whole-brain overview
explorerParts.short: All systems on one orienting map
explorerParts.detail: Orient cortex, deep structures, brainstem, cerebellum, white matter, vasculature, protective layers and distributed networks before selecting a detailed destination.
explorerParts.clinical: Begin broad, then narrow by time course, examination, laterality, pathway and mechanism.

explorerParts.label: Left hemisphere
explorerParts.short: Compare language, praxis and contralateral systems
explorerParts.detail: Inspect left cortical and subcortical organisation without assuming universal dominance.
explorerParts.clinical: Confirm individual dominance and distributed network involvement.

explorerParts.label: Right hemisphere
explorerParts.short: Compare spatial attention, prosody and contralateral systems
explorerParts.detail: Inspect right cortical and subcortical organisation within bilateral networks.
explorerParts.clinical: Neglect and awareness disorders are distributed and variable.

explorerParts.label: Healthy variation
explorerParts.detail: Compare expected variation with function and context rather than a binary normal-abnormal label.
explorerParts.clinical: A structural difference may be incidental, while dysfunction may be physiologically important without a visible lesion.

explorerParts.label: Pathology pattern
explorerParts.detail: Integrate structural, functional, developmental, vascular and degenerative patterns.
explorerParts.clinical: Diagnosis requires converging phenotype, course, examination and investigation.

explorerParts.label: Cortex, insula and cingulate
explorerParts.short: Lobes, buried cortex and medial integration
explorerParts.detail: Navigate cerebral lobes, insula, operculum and cingulate cortex.
explorerParts.clinical: Cortical functions emerge through distributed connections.

explorerParts.label: Deep nuclei, limbic and diencephalon
explorerParts.short: Thalamic, hypothalamic, striatal and limbic loops
explorerParts.detail: Navigate deep nuclei, basal-ganglia circuits, limbic system, thalamus, hypothalamus and pituitary-sellar anatomy.
explorerParts.clinical: Compact nuclei and fibres can produce mixed motor, sensory, cognitive, autonomic and endocrine patterns.

explorerParts.label: Brainstem, arousal and cranial nerves
explorerParts.short: Long tracts, nuclei and ascending regulation
explorerParts.detail: Navigate brainstem, reticular activating system and cranial nerves.
explorerParts.clinical: Crossed signs, arousal change and autonomic instability require urgent contextual assessment.

explorerParts.label: Cerebellum
explorerParts.detail: Navigate hemispheres, vermis, deep nuclei and cerebellar peduncles.
explorerParts.clinical: Interpret cognitive-affective effects with concordant neurological and network evidence.

explorerParts.label: White matter and chemical pathways
explorerParts.detail: Navigate major association, commissural and projection pathways plus neurotransmitter systems.
explorerParts.clinical: Disconnection and neuromodulation can alter intact nodes across distance.

explorerParts.label: Vasculature and arterial territories
explorerParts.detail: Navigate cerebral vessels and compare ACA, MCA, PCA and posterior-circulation territories.
explorerParts.clinical: Territory borders vary; mechanism and time course remain essential.

explorerParts.label: Functional networks
explorerParts.detail: Navigate overlapping functional-network overlays across cortical and subcortical nodes.
explorerParts.clinical: Network membership is dynamic and does not assign one psychological function to one region.

explorerParts.label: Meninges and ventricular system
explorerParts.detail: Navigate meningeal layers and ventricular-CSF anatomy.
explorerParts.clinical: Mass effect, pressure, haemorrhage, inflammation and CSF obstruction can affect distant systems.

explorerParts.label: Lesion and symptom integration
explorerParts.detail: Navigate lesion mapping after comparing laterality and healthy-pathology patterns.
explorerParts.clinical: Use anatomy to rank and test hypotheses, never to reverse-infer a diagnosis or lived experience.

quiz.question: What is the best first step when using the integrated explorer for a new clinical pattern?
options: Orient to the whole-brain pattern and time course before narrowing by laterality, pathway, network and mechanism
Choose the single region most associated with one symptom
Assume the largest overlay is causal
quiz.rationale: Broad orientation prevents premature localisation and supports structured comparison of sites, pathways, networks and mechanisms.

quiz.question: Why can a small subcortical lesion cause several deficits?
options: Compact nuclei and projection fibres serving several systems may lie close together
Every deep lesion affects the entire cortex equally
Symptoms depend only on lesion volume
quiz.rationale: Deep structures contain closely packed nuclei and fibres, so a small lesion may affect multiple connected functions.

quiz.question: What does convergence of a lesion overlay with a vascular territory and functional network establish?
options: A stronger anatomical hypothesis that still requires clinical and investigative confirmation
quiz.rationale: Converging layers improve coherence but cannot replace examination, imaging interpretation, course, differential diagnosis and context.

quiz.question: Which statement best integrates cerebellar and cortical anatomy?
options: Cerebellar effects can include coordination and connected cognitive-affective changes through cerebello-thalamo-cortical loops
The cerebellum controls cognition independently of the cerebrum
All affective symptoms localise to the vermis
Cortical function is unaffected by cerebellar connections
quiz.rationale: Cerebellar contributions are mediated through distributed loops; clinical interpretation requires neurological, temporal and network concordance.

spacedRepetition.reviewPrompt: For one clinical pattern, integrate location, laterality, white-matter pathway, functional network, vascular territory, lesion mechanism and one disconfirming alternative.

accessibility.screenReaderSummary: Integrated whole-brain explorer with fourteen selectable domains, links to all 24 completed anatomy structures, four comparison modes, pathway sequence, vascular, function, lesion and presentation overlays, and overview reset.
